messages.subject: Re: Boat survey design for flying birds
parts:
Thanks Eric! I have decided to try out a Systematic Grid for the count
points and simply transit between them as though doing parallel
transects.

But I am now having difficulties with setting up a design with different
effort in different strata. I have imported a shapefile for my overall
study area and checked that the map looks right. I then imported
another shapefile as a stratum layer under the global parent layer, and
again the map for that looks right. When I come to the Design Properties
box I can chose my stratum layer but when I go to the Effort Allocation
Tab and uncheck the 'Same effort for all strata' box, the list of my
different strata does NOT appear. If I go ahead as if it is a single
strata, then I get this message:=20

Source:D5DesPrp.PointSamplerProperties.CreateListFromFlexGrid
Internal Error number: 9
Internal Error description: "Subscript out of range"

In fact, sometimes it doesn't let me get to the Effort Allocation tab at
all and says 'An unexpected error occurred while checking the options on
this page. Please check they are valid and change any incorrect values'.

Both my shapefiles are projected as BNG and I've had no problems with
doing a design for my 'global' shapefile. Is there something I need to
do with my strata shapefile for the different polygons to be recognised?

Thanks
Linda

-----Original Message-----
From: Eric Rexstad [mailto:er...@mcs.st-and.ac.uk]=20
Sent: 30 April 2010 16:59
To: Linda Wilson
Cc: DISTANCE...@jiscmail.ac.uk
Subject: Re: [DIST-SAMP] Boat survey design for flying birds

Linda:

I can appreciate that you'd like your boat to travel in a zigzag for=20
efficiency, and that you want to do snapshots at regular intervals. =20
However, if you place your snapshots at fixed distances along the=20
transects, they probably won't end up being systematic with respect to=20
each other (because of the zigzag). Is it impractical to use the=20
Distance survey design engine (systematic grid sampling) to place a set=20=

of systematic points into your study area, then after that=20design is=20
created, connect up the pattern of points in the most efficient manner?

Your second matter about differing amounts of effort at distances=20
offshore could most simply be addressed by the stratification mechanism=20=

you describe. I believe the Mexico sample project that comes with=20
Distance is an example of placing differing amounts of sampling=20
intensity within different strata.

That's my view, but other design mavens may have more clever ideas.

Linda Wilson wrote:
> > Hello
> >
> > =20
> >
> > I am designing a boat survey to estimate tern densities. Our survey
area
> > will approximately be a coastal strip c. 40km long out to 20km
offshore,
> > which encompasses the breeding colony. As all birds will be flying, we
> > are using a snapshot count method (essentially point counts) with
> > distance bands within a 180 degree arc ahead of the boat, out to 300m.
> >
> > =20
> >
> > I would like some advice on the best way to get a systematic random
> > design for the point counts for such a boat survey. I was planning to
> > use the=20Distance programme to design zig-zag line transects within our=

> > survey area. I was then going to have the point count positions
located
> > at e.g. 1km intervals along the transect. The idea is that the boat
will
> > travel at speed between count points, but slow down to allow the count
> > to be made instantaneously.
> >
> > =20
> >
> > First question is how do I ensure that the point counts are allocated
> > randomly (but systematic)? Could I randomly assign the first count
point
> > within the first 1km of the transect, and then space them at equal
> > distance from that one?
> >
> > =20
> >
> > Secondly, there will be areas of lower density further offshore, so I
> > would like to have less effort (fewer point counts) in this area (to
> > reduce survey time). Can I simply space the point counts e.g. every
2km
> > instead of 1km in this area, if so how do I then deal with this
reduced
> > effort during analysis stages? Or do I first need to split the survey
> > area into two strata, design the zig-zag transects, and then position
> > the point counts.=20
> >
> > =20
> >
> > Or should I be doing something completely different?!
> >
> > =20
> >
> > Thanks
> >
> > Linda
